newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FORECAST - F&N interim profit seen down.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - F&N interim profit seen down.

text.p: Soft drinks conglomerate Fraser & Neave Ltd (F&N) is expected to report a fall in profit as contributions from property developments dry up, investment analysts said on Monday.
F&N is due to release its results for the six months ended March 31 1997 on Friday.

Analysts polled in the Edinburgh Financial Publishing's Estimate Directory said they expected the group to make net profits of Singapore $175 million for the financial year ending in September 30 1997, down 20 percent from 1996.
"We will see negative growth this year. It is not just the property side, the food and beverage side is not doing well," said Patrick Yau, investment analyst with Schroder Securities.
Analysts said the group's brewery operations, held under Asia Pacific Breweries Ltd (APB), were expected to see more start-up losses from China operations.
Last year, the group incurred losses of S$15.6 million from its China operations and APB started another new brewery in Hainan last month.
An analyst with a European broking firm said she also expected contributions from F&N's soft drinks operations, held through F&N Coca Cola Pte Ltd, to be lacklustre.
The group had some problem with its joint venture in Sri Lanka which was hit by a strike earlier this year. Its operations in Nepal and Pakistan are still in a start-up phase.
"At a start-up phase, the surprises for such companies is usually on the negative rather than the positive side because of all the high costs," Yau said.
But the main problem with earnings this year would be declining contributions from property development, which accounted for almost 60 percent of group pre-tax profit last year.
"F&N's property earnings peaked in 1996 and this year would see the tail end of such earnings," said Michael Ong, analyst with Soc-Gen Crosby.
The failure to replace the large chunk of earnings from property development has put a drag on the company's share price.
After touching a high of S$17.40 in February 1996, F&N's share price is now trading near its four-year low of S$10.10.

"There is concern over F&N's inability to replace its property income and also the start-up expenses for its drinks business. But it is an index stock and should find some support at current levels," Ong said.
